conviction_note: The findings sum to -1.1: the July guide rests on IATA's 1.9% traffic assumption, Q3 traffic came in about flat, and Sabre's Q3 air bookings fell 1.4% against its own flat-to-up guide. The scaled number is smaller, -0.4 (p_up 45 x abs 4.0), because the last four prints were bought (including a guidance cut on 31 Jul), Amadeus keeps beating on pricing and EBITDA, and the 17% run-up has an unknown cause and is also the free control. A guidance trim would move it far more than its usual ~1% results-day reaction.

findings.finding: Amadeus' July guide rests on IATA's 2026 traffic assumption of 1.9% (cut from 4.4%), but IATA's own Q3 series came in about flat (July +0.2%, August negative, September -0.5% with Middle East carriers -8.0%). With H1 group revenue at +5.1% cc, the bottom of 'mid-to-high single digit', the 9M release is more likely to point the guide to the low end or trim it than to firm it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 31 Jul 2026 the guide was cut and the stock still closed +0.6%, then +3.7% the next session (Yahoo AMS.MC daily bars). On 8 May 2025 the stock fell 4.4%, and Feb 2024 was -7.3%. Guide changes have moved it both ways and the market has looked through Middle East cuts.
findings.original_quote: Amadeus H1 release: "este contexto geopolítico nos ha llevado a moderar las expectativas de crecimiento ... en línea con las previsiones globales de tráfico aéreo de IATA" (this geopolitical context has led us to moderate our growth expectations, in line with IATA's global air traffic forecasts) — https://amadeus.com/es/sala-de-prensa/notas-de-prensa/amadeus-s1-2026-resultados-resilientes
findings.why_not_priced: The IATA data is public, but the stock rose 17% in the 20 sessions to the seal (51.28 on 8 Oct to 59.98) and has kept rising since IATA published on 30 Oct (56.76 to ~60). If the market expected a trim, the stock would not be making a new post-guidance-cut high into the print. This is macro-to-company transmission, so it stays small; the company tied its guide to this series itself.
findings.independence: Sabre's Q3 air bookings of -1.4% against its own flat-to-low-single-digit guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001597033/000162828026070598/q32026earningsrelease.htm) point the same way from a direct competitor, but bear on the quarter more than on the guide.

findings.finding: Sabre, the closest listed GDS peer, reported on 5 Nov that Q3 air bookings fell to 79.4m from 80.5m (-1.4%), below its own Q2 guide of 'flat to low-single-digit YoY growth' and down from +1% in Q2. This points to slightly negative Q3 Air Distribution bookings at Amadeus, which is more exposed to the Middle East.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In H1 2026 Amadeus printed air bookings -3.7%, and on the 31 Jul release the stock rose 0.6%, so weak bookings have not been punished when pricing held up.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out on 5 Nov, before the seal. AMS was +0.7% on the day (59.64 to 60.04), so at most a partial adjustment. If it had been read as a negative read-through, AMS would have dipped on the day of the peer print. Partly priced; sized small.
findings.independence: IATA September RPK -0.5% and Middle East -8.0% (https://www.iata.org/en/pressroom/2026-releases/10-30-air-passenger-falls-september/), a different source pointing the same way. It is the same industry fact as finding 1 seen from a counterparty, but it lands on the quarter rather than the guide.

findings.finding: Amadeus has beaten on profitability in both 2026 quarters despite falling volumes: Q1 EBITDA was 3% above Renta 4's estimate, and Q2 adjusted EBITDA was reported as beating consensus. Pricing is carrying the quarter (H1 revenue per booking +5.1% cc, revenue per passenger boarded +7.5% cc), and Sabre also printed a +3% booking fee and raised its EBITDA guide on 5 Nov.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Results days 8 May 2026 +1.9%, 27 Feb 2026 +2.7%, 7 Nov 2025 +1.6% (Yahoo AMS.MC daily bars); margin beats have been bought modestly.
findings.original_quote: Renta 4 headline: 'Amadeus: Resultados 1T26 que superan ligeramente las previsiones' (Amadeus: Q1 2026 results that slightly beat forecasts); Q2: 'Amadeus supera las previsiones de EBITDA pero advierte de dificultades por Oriente Medio' (Amadeus beats EBITDA forecasts but warns of Middle East difficulties) — https://es.marketscreener.com/noticias/amadeus-supera-las-previsiones-de-ebitda-pero-advierte-de-dificultades-por-oriente-medio-ce7f5bdad18ff424
findings.why_not_priced: It is a pattern, not a Q3 number, and consensus will have moved toward it. Filed small, and it partly offsets findings 1-2 on the profit line.
findings.independence: Sabre Q3 average booking fee +3% and EBITDA guide raised (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001597033/000162828026070598/q32026earningsrelease.htm).

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly negative, the same sign as the priced lean (-0.85, which here is the 20-day run-up alone), so they add little measurable over the free control. Finding 1 is the part that does not depend on the run-up, because it rests on the guide-versus-IATA gap.

lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' (guidance changes median 9.0%) and 'let reaction history move p_up, not abs_move_pct': raised abs_move_pct from 3.5 to 4.0 because a guide trim or narrowing is live, even though this name's own results-day moves run about 1%
'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction': cut the beat-pattern finding from +0.4 to +0.3, since it is a pattern rather than a Q3 number
'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series; macro-to-company is a hypothesis': kept the IATA-to-guide finding at -1.0 rather than enlarging it
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': added the FY FCF guide versus H1 FCF to new_in_release as an unknown line; no sourced number, so it is not filed as a finding
